messages.subject: Low successfully assigned fragments
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am new to RNAseq analysis and this is my first time using featureCounts. I have some sequences (PE100 from Illumina HiSeq4000), prepared with the TruSeq stranded mRNA kit and want to do differential expression analysis. I aligned my reads to the genome using TopHat2 (consistently around 75% alignment to genome), and am using the resulting accepted_hits.bam as my input into featureCounts.

This is my command for featurecounts (subread-1.5.0):
featureCounts -T 8 \
-p -F GTF -t exon -g Parent -s 2 \
-a Csinensis_154_gene.gtf \
-G Csinensis_154.fa \
-o NC1-8_featurecounts_output.txt \
accepted_hits.bam

My output shows very low successfully assigned fragments- around 20%. I also have changed -B and -M settings, but neither provide much improvement. -s 2 is correct over -s 1. Example output:

messages.subject: Re: Low successfully assigned fragments
messages.body_plain:
Hi Liz,

Firstly you do not need to specify '-G' since this option is only useful when '-J' is specified. However this doesn't affect your assignment percentage.

Having a large number of reads in category "Unassigned_Ambiguity" suggests that in your annotation many genes overlap with each other. You may try to use a different annotation to see if assignment rate improves.

Cheers,

Wei

messages.subject: subread/exactSNP in cancer DNA-seq
messages.body_plain:
Hello all,

I'm relatively new to bioinformatics, so apologies for a few, possibly obvious, questions!

1. Does anyone know if there are any comparative studies looking at the sensitivity/specificity of ExactSNP versus other callers (eg mutect or platypus), particularly in the context of sequencing cancer?

2. Is there any theoretical reason that ExactSNP might be better or worse at DNA NGS in cancer?  I ask because the bioinformaticians I've met at my institute tend to use BWA for read alignment in cancer DNA-seq, and I see the paper (Liao Y, Smyth GK and Shi W (2013). ExactSNP: an efficient and accurate SNP calling algorithm. In preparation) is still in preparation - I'm guessing it would contain some comparisons when published.  I understand other methods of calling variants use HMM, which can try to factor in some structual variation (haploid/3/4-ploid etc) when attempting to call variants - I just wonder how exactSNP signal vs noise works for this.

3. Is there any necessity / advantage to sorting the resulting BAM file prior to running exactSNP?

Many thanks in advance for your help.

All best,
Duncan.

messages.subject: subread too slow, WHY?
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I am trying to align one DNA whole genome sequence file using subread, the sequence reads are paired end, 150 bp reads. I used 'thread=64' and 216 core (9 nodes, 24 core each). But after two days it processed only 15% and I had to kill the job.

I am using the university quest, so basically I can get as many nodes/cores as I want.
